channel.title: Arjun Kanojia's blog
channel.description: Notes on running AWS and Kubernetes platforms in production.

item.title: EKS 1.34 end of standard support: a zero-downtime upgrade playbook
item.description: EKS 1.34 leaves standard support on 2 December 2026: the cost of extended support, the cluster upgrade policy, in-place versus blue/green, the Kubernetes 1.35 to 1.37 changes that break workloads, Karpenter node rotation with disruption budgets, failure modes and a two-week plan.

item.title: MCP servers are supply chain: securing the agent tool layer on EKS
item.description: Running MCP servers on EKS as production dependencies: the 2026 MCP CVE patterns, an MCP gateway with audience-bound tokens, EKS Pod Identity, signed and pinned images, default-deny egress, tool-definition drift detection, OPA policy, the OWASP MCP Top 10 and a CVE runbook.

item.title: Serving LLMs on EKS after Kubernetes 1.37: DRA, scale-to-zero and inference-aware routing
item.description: GPU inference on EKS with Kubernetes 1.37: DRA ResourceClaims with Karpenter, MIG versus time-slicing, Gateway API Inference Extension routing, HPA scale-to-zero and cold starts, gang scheduling status, device taints, failure modes and a rollout checklist.

item.title: From IDP to agentic developer platform: golden paths as contracts agents can run
item.description: Turning golden paths into contracts AI agents can run: Backstage MCP actions, Crossplane v2 XRDs, deterministic validation gates, Kargo promotions with pull requests and verification, autonomy levels per path, failure modes, metrics and a 60-day plan.

item.title: AI SRE agents on call: an autonomy ladder for incident response
item.description: Where an AI agent belongs in incident response: a five-level autonomy ladder, read-only Kubernetes and AWS identities, an action catalogue gated by OPA policy, failure modes, promotion metrics and a 90-day rollout plan.

item.title: Guardrails for AI agents writing Terraform: OIDC, OPA and approval gates
item.description: A guardrail design for AI agents that write Terraform: no cloud credentials in the agent workspace, plan-only and apply-only OIDC roles, OPA policy on the plan JSON, GitLab CI approval gates, autonomy tiers by blast radius and drift detection.

item.title: Surviving peak traffic on EKS: architecture, KEDA, Karpenter and DR drills
item.description: Akamai, EKS, MongoDB, Kafka, Aerospike and RDS under a traffic spike: k6 load testing, KEDA and Karpenter pre-scaling, DR strategies, backup-restore and failover drills, and an event-day runbook.
